canonical_fact: JAM state maps 32-bit service identifiers to service accounts containing storage, preimage state, code identity, balances, supervision and execution metadata.
misconceptions: A JAM service account contains only code and has no protocol-visible storage or balance.

relations.statement: Service storage is one component of a service account.
Preimage lookup state is another component of a service account.
The service code identified by the account exposes Refine as entry point 0.
The service code identified by the account exposes Accumulate as entry point 1.

title: Service account

canonical_fact: A JAM service identifier is a 32-bit unsigned value used as the key for service accounts.
title: Service identifier

canonical_fact: A service account stores a hash identifying its code-and-metadata preimage; a functional service must make the corresponding preimage available.

relations.statement: The service code hash must resolve to code and metadata through the service preimage lookup for the service to be functional.

title: Service code hash

canonical_fact: A service has arbitrary key/value storage that is mutable during on-chain accumulation.
misconceptions: Service storage is directly readable during arbitrary in-core Refine execution as the latest global state.
title: Service storage

canonical_fact: A service account has a token balance that also participates in storage-footprint threshold requirements.
title: Service balance

canonical_fact: Service code entry point 0 is Refine: it executes in-core and is essentially stateless, apart from access to defined historical/preimage context.
misconceptions: Refine directly mutates the global JAM state.

relations.statement: Refinement executes a work item's service logic to contribute to a work report.
Refine is separated from the stateful Accumulate entry point.

title: Refine entry point

canonical_fact: Service code entry point 1 is Accumulate: it executes on-chain and may mutate protocol-visible service state.
misconceptions: Accumulate is the stateless off-chain phase.
title: Accumulate entry point

canonical_fact: A service account records the minimum gas required per work item to invoke its Accumulate entry point.
title: Minimum accumulate gas

canonical_fact: A service account records the minimum gas required when its Accumulate logic is invoked for a deferred transfer.
title: Minimum memo gas

canonical_fact: A service can expose static data by hash through its preimage lookup so that the data can later be available to in-core Refine execution.
misconceptions: Preimage lookup is identical to mutable service storage.

relations.statement: Lookup-anchor history makes preimage availability deterministic for Refine.

title: Preimage lookup

canonical_fact: A service's preimage-request state tracks requested preimages and the times at which they became available or unavailable.
title: Preimage request

canonical_fact: Historical lookup determines whether a service preimage was available at a specified recent timeslot and returns it when the availability history permits.
title: Historical lookup

canonical_fact: Refine uses a recently finalized historical state, the lookup anchor, so validators can agree which service preimages were available for in-core execution.
misconceptions: Refine always reads the latest head state.

relations.statement: A work context identifies the lookup anchor used to make Refine inputs historically determinate.

title: Lookup anchor

canonical_fact: General storage is arbitrary mutable on-chain key/value state, while preimage lookup is hash-addressed static data with explicit historical availability semantics for Refine.
title: Preimage versus storage

canonical_fact: A service's storage footprint counts items and octets from storage and preimage request state for balance/deposit accounting.
title: Service storage footprint

canonical_fact: A service has a minimum balance determined from base, item and byte deposits minus any gratis storage allowance.
title: Threshold balance

canonical_fact: JAM state designates privileged service roles including manager, delegator, registrar, per-core authorizer assigners and always-accumulating services.

relations.statement: Manager is one of JAM’s privileged service roles.
Per-core assigners are privileged services that control authorizer queues.

title: Service privileges

canonical_fact: The manager service may alter protocol privilege assignments and grant storage-deposit credits.
title: Manager service

canonical_fact: The delegator service may set the staging validator key sequence.
title: Delegator service

canonical_fact: The registrar service alone may create new service accounts using protected service-index ranges.
title: Registrar service

canonical_fact: Each core has a privileged assigner service capable of altering that core's authorizer queue.
title: Authorizer assigner service

canonical_fact: Each service has a supervisor; non-privileged mutating operations on a service are authorized through its effective supervisor, and a service may supervise itself.
misconceptions: Every service must be supervised by a different privileged system service.

relations.statement: Supervisor authority creates a conflict rule when supervisor and service mutate the same state in one accumulation round.

title: Service supervisor
